definitions.gloss: far right; extreme right wing (in politics)
definitions.explanation: A political label for the extreme right end of the ideological spectrum — parties, groups, or individuals associated with strong nationalism, anti-immigration positions, or hardline conservatism. Used in news reporting, commentary, and academic writing about politics worldwide.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{極右|きょくう}の{政治家|せいじか}だ。
{選挙|せんきょ}で{極右|きょくう}{政党|せいとう}が{票|ひょう}を{伸|の}ばした。
examples.english: A far-right party gained votes in the election.

examples.japanese: ヨーロッパでは{近年|きんねん}、{極右|きょくう}{勢力|せいりょく}の{台頭|たいとう}が{懸念|けねん}されている。
examples.english: In Europe there has been growing concern in recent years about the rise of far-right forces.

notes:
Literally "extreme right," from {極|きょく} (extreme, pole) and {右|う} (right). The word is neutral in form but almost always critical in context — speakers who use it are typically distancing themselves from the groups they describe. In Japanese political discourse it is sometimes also used for hardline nationalist or street-activist groups.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {極右|きょくう}{政党|せいとう}: far-right political party
- {極右|きょくう}{勢力|せいりょく}: far-right forces
- {極右|きょくう}{思想|しそう}: far-right ideology
- {極右|きょくう}の{台頭|たいとう}: the rise of the far right
- {極右|きょくう}と{呼|よ}ばれる: to be called far-right

RELATED WORDS:
- {極左|きょくさ}: far left — direct antonym
- {右翼|うよく}: right wing — broader term covering the full right of the spectrum
- {保守|ほしゅ}: conservative — the mainstream right
- ネオナチ: neo-Nazi — a specific variety of far-right group
